clue.text: Set up a partnership

blocks.note: first meaning: to place something upright
second meaning: in cricket, the runs two batsmen add together while both are in

explanation.surface: Two people agree to go into business together.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a partnership between two batsmen is also called a stand; the surface makes it sound like founding a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To put upright is one verb sense, and the cricketing term for a batting pair's combined innings is the noun.

clue.text: Runs in country getting injury

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a European country

explanation.surface: A jogger abroad twists an ankle while out running.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside SPAIN to make SPRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a wrenching injury to a joint's ligaments.

clue.text: Tolerant? Waspish? Possibly a mild rebuke is the answer

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters before it can be reordered

blocks.note: the letters of both words, taken together

explanation.surface: Torn between leniency and sharpness, the answer is a gentle reprimand.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface neatly matches the answer: a mild punishment sits between tolerant and waspish.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a token punishment, a light telling-off rather than a serious penalty.

clue.text: Cheese in buns he laid out

indicators.note: laid out suggests spread around in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A baker puts cheese in the rolls he has set out on the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a soft blue-veined cheese from Denmark.

clue.text: Actual money to be made if top rent adjusted

indicators.note: something adjusted has been altered, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A landlord muses on what he would really earn if the highest rent were changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Net profit is what remains after costs, the real money earned rather than gross takings.

clue.text: Ascot's winning margin, then dead heat?

blocks.note: a horse can win by a neck
a dead heat is a tie; then simply orders the pieces

explanation.surface: A race at Ascot is won by a neck, then ends in a dead heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot reads as the racecourse, but here it is the wide cravat named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neckcloth or cravat, a kind of tie worn at the neck.

clue.text: Silk from refurbished US store

indicators.note: a refurbished shop has been redone, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: An American shop, newly done up, sells silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse brownish silk from wild silkworms, also spelt tussah.

clue.text: Part of film is serious, according to report ...

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: real, as in genuine and not joking

explanation.surface: Part of a film is reported to be serious.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool of film, and a feature is made of several of them.

clue.text: ... film total art fanatic misconstrued

indicators.note: something misconstrued is read wrongly, so the letters are taken in a wrong order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A film buff misreads a picture, continuing from the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to 6-down, both clues about film.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal Attraction is a 1987 thriller starring Michael Douglas and Glenn Close.

clue.text: Develop film showing traitor

blocks.note: to turn into something is to develop into it
a thin film or layer, as of paint

explanation.surface: Processing a roll of film exposes a traitor, as in a spy story.
explanation.walkthrough: Develop film reads as a photographic phrase, but each word supplies a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who deserts one side for the other, so a traitor.

clue.text: Take corners well racing in Jersey?

indicators.note: racing letters dash about, so they end up in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Advice for a driver competing on the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the Channel Island; it is the knitted garment, and the question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted pullover, and one with a high folded collar is an example of the type.

clue.text: One male job in tax

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for male
a post or job

explanation.surface: A man with one job is caught up in tax matters.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposition is a levy or duty imposed by authority, so a tax.

clue.text: Endlessly hinder alliance

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to block is to obstruct or hinder

explanation.surface: Someone keeps obstructing an alliance at every turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties combined for a common purpose.

clue.text: Bone in arm, at least cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An X-ray report: at least one bone in the arm is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the bone in the arm, but the answer is in the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A metatarsal is one of the five long bones of the foot.

clue.text: Powerless, locked in sauna, bleeding

indicators.note: locked in says the word is shut up inside the following text

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A victim shut in a sauna, bleeding and helpless.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable means lacking the power or means to do something.

clue.text: Choose artist to illustrate a type of complex

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
RA, Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: Picking an artist to illustrate a psychology text.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electra complex is a psychoanalytic term for a girl's attachment to her father, so Electra names a kind of complex.

clue.text: Rich source of oil, also buried diamonds

indicators.note: something buried is put inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: an oil well
too means also
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An oil source, with diamonds buried too: the stuff of riches.
explanation.walkthrough: Source of oil looks like part of the rich definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is the single word at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do is an idiom for comfortably wealthy.

clue.text: Wear out car part

blocks.note: first meaning: to tire completely
second meaning: the pipe that carries away engine gases

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a part wearing out on a car; the verb and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to drain of energy; as a noun it is the tailpipe system of a vehicle.

clue.text: Start trip

blocks.note: first meaning: to set something off
second meaning: to activate a switch or mechanism

explanation.walkthrough: Start trip suggests setting off on a journey, but trip is the verb for setting off an alarm or switch.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger is to set in motion, and also to release a catch, as one trips a switch.

clue.text: Lean, adult leader of group diving into lake

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
diving into something puts it inside that thing

blocks.note: a mere is a lake
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
the first letter of group

explanation.surface: A slim grown-up, heading a team, plunges into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A and G go together inside MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or thin, the same sense as lean when describing a ration or a year.

clue.text: Malicious assertions over apartment in area of seaside land

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

blocks.note: mud is slander, as in mudslinging
a flat is an apartment

explanation.surface: Spiteful gossip about someone's flat in a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A mud flat is a stretch of muddy coastal ground exposed at low tide.

clue.text: Queen of Persia belonging to Xerxes, there?

indicators.note: belonging to says the word is part of the following text

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A question about which Persian queen was Xerxes's.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer: in the Bible, Esther became the wife of King Xerxes (Ahasuerus).
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Esther tells of the Jewish woman who became queen to the Persian king.

clue.text: Fine linen from Prestatyn, Wales, sent over

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the following words
sent over means flipped, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the town and the start of the country

explanation.surface: Linen dispatched from a seaside town in north Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Prestatyn is a resort town on the north Wales coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn is a very fine, sheer linen or cotton fabric.

clue.text: Obstacles in rear by travelling cranes

indicators.note: travelling letters move about and so change their order

blocks.note: hind means rear, as in hind legs
the letters of this word

explanation.surface: Mobile cranes get in the way at the back of a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindrances are things that hold back progress, so obstacles.

clue.text: Children on the radio give up

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: seed in the old sense of offspring

explanation.surface: Children listening to the radio give up on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed means descendants, as in the Bible's 'Abraham and his seed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield territory or a right.

clue.text: Writer of musical tale, we hear, receiving top prizes

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound
receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's musical of Oliver Twist
gold medals are the top prizes
a myth is a tale

explanation.surface: A musical's story wins awards, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The prizes sit inside the sound-alike pair, splitting the musical's name from the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith was the 18th-century Irish author of The Vicar of Wakefield and She Stoops to Conquer.

clue.text: In succession to throne, displaced head of Tudors

indicators.note: displaced letters are moved from their positions into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the letters of both words
the first letter of Tudors

explanation.surface: A Tudor monarch is ousted in the line of succession to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Succession reads as royal inheritance, but the definition means one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: On the trot is a British idiom for consecutively, as in three wins on the trot.

clue.text: Solitary type Cockney fellow dismissed

indicators.note: someone dismissed is sent away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a Cockney is a native Londoner
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A lonely Cockney man has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: DON is taken out of the middle of LONDONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is a person who prefers to be alone, a solitary sort.
